drug_class: Low Molecular Weight Heparin (Blood Thinner / Anticoagulant)
purpose: Dalteparin is a blood thinner used to prevent and treat dangerous blood clots in your veins or lungs. It is also used to reduce the risk of clotting in people who have had a heart attack or certain heart conditions. Doctors also prescribe it to prevent clots in people who are on bedrest or having surgery.
how_it_works: Your blood naturally clots to stop bleeding, but sometimes clots form inside your veins or arteries where they should not be. Dalteparin works by blocking certain proteins in your blood that help clots form, making it harder for dangerous clots to develop or grow larger. Think of it as turning down the dial on your blood's clotting system to keep things flowing safely.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is bruising, pain, redness, or irritation at the injection site where you give yourself the shot. You may also notice some minor bleeding, such as bleeding gums or a nosebleed. Some people experience a small drop in their platelet count, which your doctor will monitor with blood tests.
warnings: Because this medicine thins your blood, it can cause serious bleeding — tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual bruising, blood in your urine or stool, coughing up blood, or bleeding that won't stop. A rare but serious condition called HIT (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia) can occur, where the medicine actually causes dangerous clotting, so watch for sudden swelling or pain in your legs. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, and always tell all your healthcare providers that you are on a blood thinner before any procedure or surgery.
typical_dosing: Dalteparin is given as an injection just under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually once or twice a day depending on your condition and body weight. Your doctor or nurse will show you exactly how to give yourself the injection at home. The dose is carefully calculated based on your weight and the reason you are taking it, so never adjust your dose on your own.
